validated_results.title: Well-done meat consumption, NAT1 and NAT2 acetylator genotypes and prostate cancer risk: the multiethnic cohort study.
validated_results.journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
validated_results.reason: Nested case-control study within the Multiethnic Cohort reporting well-done (red) meat intake and incident prostate cancer risk, with exposure effects reported separately from genotypes.

extraction.comparison_type: Preference for and intake of well-done (red) meat versus lower intake/preference
extraction.ethnicity: African American, Native Hawaiian, Japanese American, Latino, and Caucasian
extraction.population: Men in the Multiethnic Cohort study

sample_size.excerpt: Cases (n = 2,106) and controls (n = 2,063) were genotyped for eight single nucleotide polymorphisms in NAT1 and seven single nucleotide polymorphisms in NAT2 that characterized all common alleles for these genes.
sample_size.location: abstract, methods sentence; total_n derived from reported group counts 2106 + 2063 = 4169

cases.excerpt: Cases (n = 2,106) and controls (n = 2,063) were genotyped for eight single nucleotide polymorphisms in NAT1 and seven single nucleotide polymorphisms in NAT2 that characterized all common alleles for these genes.

comparison.excerpt: There was no evidence of an increased risk associated with preference for well-done meat, intake of well-done meat

design.excerpt: in a case-control study of PC nested within the Multiethnic Cohort study

continent.excerpt: Prostate cancer (PC) is the most common male malignancy in the United States

ethnicity.excerpt: among five ethnicities (African American, Native Hawaiian, Japanese American, Latino, and Caucasian)

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Well-done meat intake was computed based on responses to a detailed food frequency questionnaire including a question on meat preference.

parallel_r3_gate_reasons: important quantitative evidence remains missing or invalid: ci_lower, ci_upper, effect_size, effect_type, p_value

validated_results.title: Plasma metabolic profiling reveals age-dependency of systemic effects of green tea polyphenols in mice with and without prostate cancer.
validated_results.reason: The study administered green tea polyphenols exclusively to TRAMP and wild-type mice with metabolic profiling, providing no human incidence data.

validated_results.title: Plasma metabolic profiling reveals age-dependency of systemic effects of green tea polyphenols in mice with and without prostate cancer.
validated_results.reason: This is a preclinical mouse experiment of dietary green tea polyphenols with no human participants or incident prostate cancer outcomes.

validated_results.title: Ginkgo biloba and risk of cancer: secondary analysis of the Ginkgo Evaluation of Memory (GEM) Study.
validated_results.reason: Randomized placebo-controlled trial of Ginkgo biloba extract supplementation reporting a site-specific hazard ratio for incident prostate cancer.

extraction.comparison_type: 120 mg twice-daily Ginkgo extract (EGb 761) versus placebo
extraction.population: GEM Study participants 75+ years of age

sample_size.excerpt: A total of 3069 GEM participants 75+ years of age were randomized to twice-daily doses of either 120 mg Ginkgo extract (EGb 761) or placebo and followed for a median 6.1 years.

effect_size.excerpt: Among the site-specific cancers analyzed, we observed an increased risk of breast (HR, 2.15; 95%CI, 0.97-4.80; p = 0.06) and colorectal (HR, 1.62; 95%CI, 0.92-2.87; p = 0.10) cancer, and a reduced risk of prostate cancer (HR, 0.71; 95%CI, 0.43-1.17; p = 0.18).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Among the site-specific cancers analyzed, we observed an increased risk of breast (HR, 2.15; 95%CI, 0.97-4.80; p = 0.06) and colorectal (HR, 1.62; 95%CI, 0.92-2.87; p = 0.10) cancer, and a reduced risk of prostate cancer (HR, 0.71; 95%CI, 0.43-1.17; p = 0.18).

comparison.excerpt: randomized to twice-daily doses of either 120 mg Ginkgo extract (EGb 761) or placebo

design.excerpt: the largest randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial of Ginkgo supplementation to date
